exposure: duration of disease longer than 9 years
cohort: 132 pregnancies in 95 women with rheumatic diseases (RDs)
finding: Pregnancies with RDs were at increased risk of having both maternal complications and adverse neonatal outcomes, indicating these pregnancies should be closely monitored.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with rheumatic diseases experienced a higher rate of emergency cesarean sections and preterm deliveries compared to the general obstetric population.
birth_weight: SLE: 2591 g, APS: 2600 g, GOP: 2950 g
